top_stories.title: Binance Suffers Record $6.34B Hack Linked to North Korea
points: $6.34 billion drained from Binance hot wallets (liquid cryptocurrency stored online for trading) in the largest exchange hack in crypto history.
Blockchain investigators (TRM Labs and Chainalysis) attribute the theft to North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor.
Binance is setting aside its full $6.34 billion reserve to compensate affected users, with CEO Richard Teng stating no customer funds are ultimately at risk.
Attack exploited EIP-7702, an Ethereum feature letting wallets temporarily delegate transaction approval to smart contracts, to bypass normal security controls.

Tether and Circle froze about $3 billion in stolen stablecoins before withdrawal, though the attacker converted some funds to harder-to-trace Ethereum via Uniswap and took loans against USDT on Aave (a crypto lending protocol).
Breach involved multiple entry points, starting with a compromised engineer's laptop and revealing additional vulnerabilities in Binance's infrastructure.
Binance aims to reopen withdrawals by Sunday while investigating and patching security gaps.
Bitcoin fell 5.4% and Ethereum fell 5.9% within 24 hours of the hack news.

unique_angles.point: Global regulators are evaluating potential enforcement actions and penalties against Binance in response to the breach.
Incident expected to trigger renewed scrutiny of exchange security standards and influence future regulatory oversight of centralized platforms.

items.title: Trezor Warns of Counterfeit Hardware Wallets
points: Trezor received a credible report of a malicious hardware implant (hidden chip) in a Safe 5 wallet bought from reseller CryptoBilis.
Attack vector resembles a previous hack that cost Ledger wallet users $86 million.
Trezor advises all affected buyers to move funds immediately, even though it has not yet examined the compromised device itself.

issues.subject: Binance hit by biggest hack ever 👨‍💻

headlines: Binance suffers $6.4 billion hack—largest in crypto history—but covers all losses with its own $6.34 billion reserve fund and plans to reopen by Sunday.

North Korean group TraderTraitor blamed for the theft by blockchain investigators TRM Labs and Chainalysis, using an Ethereum feature called EIP-7702 (a mechanism that lets wallets delegate their transaction approval to smart contracts) to bypass security controls.
About $3 billion in stolen funds already frozen as Tether and Circle moved quickly to prevent stablecoin withdrawal, though attacker converted some to harder-to-track Ethereum.
Trezor warns buyers of counterfeit hardware wallets from reseller CryptoBilis after credible report of hidden malicious chips, similar to a previous $86 million Ledger hack.

sections.title: The Binance Hack: What Happened
points: $6.4 billion drained from Binance hot wallets (liquid cryptocurrency stored online for trading) Thursday afternoon in the largest exchange hack ever recorded.
Attack involved multiple breach points, not a single entry—started with a compromised engineer's laptop but later revealed additional vulnerabilities in Binance's security infrastructure.
Attacker exploited EIP-7702, an Ethereum feature allowing wallets to delegate control temporarily, bypassing normal approval controls that would normally require additional authentication steps.

Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze approximately $3 billion before it could be withdrawn, but attacker outpaced freezes by swapping stable tokens for unfreezable Ethereum on Uniswap and taking loans against USDT on Aave (a lending protocol).

sections.title: Response & Recovery
points: CEO Richard Teng announced Binance set aside $6.34 billion to fully cover user losses—no customer funds at risk despite the theft.
Exchange aims to reopen withdrawals by Sunday as it investigates multiple security breaches and implements fixes.
Market reacted sharply: Bitcoin dropped 5.4% and Ethereum fell 5.9% within 24 hours on hack news.

sections.title: Hardware Wallet Warning
points: Trezor received credible report of malicious hardware implant in Safe 5 wallet purchased from reseller CryptoBilis, using same attack vector as previous Ledger hack.
Trezor advises all affected buyers to move funds immediately despite not yet examining the compromised device itself.
